(8 April 2012) |matches=240 |total goals=458 |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance=20,409{{Cite web|url=http://sportsnewsarena.com/gor-mahia-fans-help-double-kpl-ticket-revenues|title = Gor Mahia fans help double KPL ticket revenues}} ([[Gor Mahia]] versus [[AFC Leopards]]) |prevseason=[[2011 Kenyan Premier League|2011]] |nextseason=[[2013 Kenyan Premier League|2013]] }} The '''2012 Kenyan Premier League''' (known as the [[Tusker (African beer)|Tusker]] Premier League for sponsorship reasons) was the ninth season of the [[Kenyan Premier League]] since its establishment in 2003 and the forty-ninth season of top division [[Association football|football]] in [[Kenya]] since 1963. It began on 11 February with [[Tusker F.C.|Tusker]] and [[Nairobi City Stars]] and ended on 10 November with [[Oserian F.C.|Oserian]] and [[Rangers F.C. (Kenya)|Rangers]]. The winners of the league will earn a place at the preliminary round of the [[2013 CAF Champions League]] and play against the [[2012 FKF President's Cup]] champions at the [[2013 Kenyan Super Cup (pre-season)|2013 Kenyan Super Cup]]. The defending champions [[Tusker F.C.|Tusker]], who also became the defending champions of the [[Kenyan Super Cup]] after beating [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]], the defending champions of the [[FKF Cup]], [[2012 Kenyan Super Cup|earlier in the year]], won their tenth league title after beating [[Nairobi City Stars]] 3−0 away at the [[Hope Centre]]. [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]], the former league leaders with 58 points (Tusker were second with 57), needed a win against [[Thika United F.C.|Thika United]] to clinch a record thirteenth title, but the match ended in a 1−1 draw. [[A.F.C. Leopards]], who were third with 57 points (Tusker were ahead on [[goal difference]]), also needed a win for a chance at a record thirteenth title as well, but lost 1−0 away to [[Chemelil Sugar F.C.|Chemelil Sugar]]. A total of 16 teams are competed for the league, with fourteen returning from the 2011 season and one promoted from the [[FKL Nationwide League]] and the [[KFF Nationwide League]], which were joint to make [[FKF Division One]] after the 2011 season. FKL champions [[Oserian F.C.|Oserian]] and KFF champions [[Muhoroni Youth F.C.|Muhoroni Youth]] were promoted, while [[Congo JMJ United F.C.|Congo JMJ United]] and [[Bandari F.C. (Kenyan football club)|Bandari]], finishing last and second-last respectively, were relegated. Oserian were relegated at the end of the season, along with [[Rangers F.C. (Kenya)|Rangers]]. The league was halted at the end of 20 May to give teams a chance to rest and make possible changes in their squads during the mid-year [[transfer window]]. Matches resumed on 23 June. On 21 August, the Kenyan Premier League and [[East African Breweries]] signed a [[Kenyan shilling|KSh]] 170 million/= ([[United States dollar|US$]]2.02 million; £1.28 million [[Pound sterling|sterling]]; [[Euro|€]]1.62 million) deal to rename the league to the '''[[Tusker (African beer)|Tusker]] Premier League''', making it the most lucrative deal in Kenyan football history.{{cite web |url=http://www.capitalfm.co.ke/sports/2012/08/21/kpl-now-tusker-pl-in-sh170m-deal/ |title=KPL now Tusker PL in Sh170m deal |publisher=[[98.4 Capital FM]] |date=21 August 2012 |accessdate=21 August 2012}} ==Changes from last season== {{location map+ |Kenya |float=right |width=380 |caption=Locations of the 2012 Kenyan Premier League teams.|places= {{location map~ |Kenya |lat=-0.077675 |long=35.130832 |label=
